wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 알고리즘(algorithms)이 '이용되는' 대상이므로 진행형 수동태를 구성하는 'being employed'는 어법상 옳다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 선행사인 rare diseases를 수식하며 뒤에 주어가 빠진 불완전한 절을 이끄는 주격 관계대명사 'that'은 어법상 옳다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): even if가 이끄는 조건절 내의 주어가 단수 명사인 'a disease'이므로 단수 동사 'is'는 어법상 옳다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 과거분사형 형용사인 'neglected'를 수식하기 위해 부사 'traditionally'가 쓰인 것은 어법상 옳다.

question.explanation: (D) "have been neglected"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "has been neglected"로 고쳐야 한다. 이 문장의 주절 주어는 단수 명사인 'the disease'이며, 'compared to First World illnesses'는 부사구에 불과합니다. 따라서 동격 또는 수식 구조를 걷어낸 진짜 주어 'the disease'에 맞추어 단수 동사인 'has been neglected'가 와야 하므로, 복수형 조동사를 사용한 'have been neglected'는 비문입니다. 바로 앞에 위치한 복수 명사 'illnesses'에 이끌려 수일치를 혼동하지 않도록 주의해야 합니다.
question.passageWithMarkers: In the pharmaceutical industry, algorithms are __(A) being employed__ to find treatments and drugs for rare diseases __(B) that__ to date haven't received much attention. The hard truth has always been that pharma devotes more research and development resources to diseases that affect the rich. The definition of rare has too often been associated with poor ― that __(C) is__, even if a disease is quite prevalent in a population that cannot afford to pay for it (for example, people living in the developing world), the disease __(D) have been neglected__ compared to First World illnesses. By lowering the cost of data collection, mining, and analysis in drug development and clinical trials, AI can help offset imbalances in the pharmaceutical industry that direct attention to diseases that "pay," whether because the disease is more common or because it is prevalent among demographics that can pay more. We see the democratizing power of AI to broaden the attention of the medical and research communities to find cures to __(E) traditionally__ neglected health issues and among traditionally neglected populations.

question.passageWithMarkers: To minimize building costs and maximize revenues, skyscrapers generally take the shape of squares or rectangles. These are not particularly aerodynamic shapes, and this results in a wind phenomenon __(A) called__ "vortex shedding." As wind meets a rectangular skyscraper it pushes on the flat face of the building before flowing around its sides, __(B) where__ eventually it separates from the face of the structure. The difference in pressures on the front and back faces of the building gives rise to vortices, or spinning currents of wind, __(C) what__ flow downstream from the building. The vortices pull and push the building in a direction perpendicular to the wind at frequencies that can become dangerously self-sustaining. To minimize vortex shedding, skyscraper designers do everything in their powers to confuse the wind. Orienting the building so that the longer face of the structure __(D) is__ parallel with prevailing winds can help. Chopping or rounding off corners of a building can likewise make it more __(E) aerodynamic__. Roughing up the corners of the building through the careful placement of balconies or stepped corners can help by disturbing or delaying the formation of strong vortices.

question.passageWithMarkers: To minimize building costs and maximize revenues, skyscrapers generally take the shape of squares or rectangles. These are not particularly aerodynamic shapes, and this results in a wind phenomenon called "vortex shedding." As wind meets a rectangular skyscraper it pushes on the flat face of the building before flowing around its sides, where eventually it separates from the face of the structure. The difference in pressures on the front and back faces of the building gives rise to vortices, or __(A) spinning__ currents of wind, that flow downstream from the building. The vortices pull and push the building in a direction perpendicular to the wind at frequencies __(B) that__ can become dangerously self-sustaining. To minimize vortex shedding, skyscraper designers do everything in __(C) their__ powers to confuse the wind. Orienting the building so that the longer face of the structure is parallel with prevailing winds can help. Chopping or rounding off corners of a building can likewise make it more __(D) aerodynamic__. Roughing up the corners of the building through the careful placement of balconies or stepped corners can help by __(E) to disturb__ or delaying the formation of strong vortices.
